title: The Limits of Centralized Pricing in Online Marketplaces and the Value of User Control
eligible_reason: No staggered design. The main evidence is a randomized field experiment on a peer-to-peer car rental platform (treatment vs control providers). Section 4 adds a 2x2 difference-in-differences comparing platform-wide revenue and hours rented around a single market-wide imposition of centralized pricing with the same weeks of the prior year (y = b0 + b1 Post + b2 Trt + b3 Post x Trt, Trt = actual year), collapsed to pre/post window aggregates (centralizing.tex lines 533-613). One adoption date and no unit panel.
design_notes: analysis/3_2_did_cross.R reads data/did_cross_revenue.rds and did_cross_hoursrented.rds, which hold fitted lfe models for window sizes 2/4/6/8 weeks (README lines 244-249; Figure 4.2 and Appendix Tables 14-17). 3_1_did_lgtd_total.R plots weekly sums for actual and prior year (Figure 4.1); 3_3_did_lgtd_diffs.R gives the pre-trend test (Appendix Table 3, Figure 9). Experiment scripts 2_1_* and 2_2_* use user-level outcome files.
data_access: proprietary (platform data); authors share user-level averages and fitted models under an approved data-disclosure exception
data_files_note: README: proprietary data; authors share weekly averages and per-user aggregates without perturbation. The DiD regression input data are not shipped, only the fitted model objects.
software_notes: R (lfe, stargazer); Makefile builds the paper.
screener_notes: Screened from package. The package includes the paper's LaTeX source (centralizing.tex), used as article text.
